name: Example: Determining the Function on Which to Apply a Root-Finding Method When Applying the Implicit Euler Method
problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
y' = y^3 - x\,y, \qquad y(1)=1
$$

Using the implicit Euler method with step size $\Delta x = 1,$ the new value $y_\text{new}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g(y_\text{new}) = 0$ at each step.
Which of the following is the **specific function** $g(y_\text{new})$ used in the first step?

- $g(y_\text{new}) = (y_\text{new})^3 - 3y_\text{new} - 1$

- $g(y_\text{new}) = 3y_\text{new} - (y_\text{new})^3 + 1$

- $g(y_\text{new}) = 3y_\text{new} - (y_\text{new})^3 - 1$

- $g(y_\text{new}) = y_\text{new} - (y_\text{new})^3 + x_\text{new}y_\text{new}$
worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
y' = f(x,y), \qquad y_0 = y(x_0),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $\Delta x$ is given by

$$
\Delta y = y'_\text{new} \cdot \Delta x,
$$

with $y'_\text{new} = f(x_\text{new},y_\text{new})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general, $\Delta y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}-{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & =({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}-{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into $y_\text{new} = y + \Delta y$ and move all terms to the left-hand side and define the resulting expression as $g(y_\text{new}){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}-{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {{{y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}+{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}}-y}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $\Delta x = 1$ is

$$
g(y_\text{new}) = y_\text{new} - (y_\text{new})^3 + x_\text{new}y_\text{new} - y.
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is $x_\text{new} = x + \Delta x = 1 + 1 = 2.$ Therefore, the function used in the first step is

$$
\begin{aligned}g({y}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}+2{y}_{\text{new}}-1 \\  & =3{y}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}-1.\end{aligned}
$$
